transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thanks. Well, what finally made me ask for help is that I just keep forgetting these little things I normally handle fine. Like returning calls... which is pretty bad because I'm a secretary. My desk is right by the front door at the office, and the draft in there is terrible, honestly. I had to bring in a space heater last week because my feet were freezing all day. My cat actually loves to sleep right in front of it when I bring it back home on the weekends, he just curls up into a little ball... 

Oh, but anyway, I've just been dropping the ball on regular stuff. Like, I'll completely forget to turn in a registration form, or I'll tell myself I need to stop for an errand on the way home, and I just drive straight past the store. I don't know why it's happening so much lately.
Are you noticing any of these memory problems at home, outside of your job as a secretary?

At home? Um... well, the errand thing I mentioned, I guess. Like forgetting to stop at the store. But mostly I'm just so tired when I get home. My husband usually handles the cooking, thank goodness. He makes this amazing chicken cacciatore, it's his grandmother's recipe. She came over from Italy when she was, like, twelve? Or maybe fourteen. I think they settled in New Jersey first, which is funny because my sister just moved to New Jersey for a new job. She's in marketing. She loves it, but the traffic there is just unbelievable. I went to visit her last month and we sat on the turnpike for an hour just trying to get to the mall. We were going to look for a dress for my cousin's wedding, but by the time we got there all the good stores were closing. So... wait, what did you ask me? Something about home?
Do you remember the things you forgot later, like the errand or the registration form, after someone reminds you or you see a reminder?

Um, well... usually I don't really remember them at all, honestly. Like, if my boss asks me about the form, I just draw a complete blank. It's like it never even happened. Which is so frustrating, because I used to be really good at keeping track of things. I mean, I have this whole color-coded filing system at work that I set up myself. I used these bright neon folders—pink for urgent, green for financial stuff, yellow for general correspondence. I actually had to go to three different office supply stores to find the exact shade of pink I wanted. The first place only had this weird salmon color, and the second place was completely sold out of pink altogether. Can you believe that? Who buys out all the pink folders? Anyway, the third place finally had them, but the cashier was so rude when I asked her to check the back for more. She just rolled her eyes at me. I mean, customer service these days is just terrible, right? Like, nobody cares anymore. Oh, but... wait, I'm sorry. Did that answer your question about the reminders?
Have you had trouble learning new things recently, like a new task or a new procedure at work?

New things? Um, no, not really. I haven't really had to learn anything new lately. My job is pretty routine, which I usually like. Although, they did just update our phone system last month. It's one of those fancy VoIP things where the calls come through the computer now instead of a regular phone. I actually really hate it because the headset they gave me pinches my ears. I tried adjusting it, but it just feels so cheap. I even asked my boss if I could bring my own from home—I have this really nice gaming headset my nephew left at my house over Christmas. He's super into those online games, you know? The ones where they all talk to each other and yell at the screen. I don't get it, honestly. He spent his whole vacation just glued to his laptop in our guest room. We tried to get him to come ice skating with us, but he said his ankles were too weak. Weak ankles! Can you imagine? He's fourteen! When I was fourteen I was doing gymnastics every single day after school. I could do a back handspring all the way across the gym floor. But anyway, yeah, I haven't had any trouble learning new things, just the regular stuff I keep dropping the ball on.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood lately?

Mood? Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I get frustrated with myself for forgetting things, obviously, but I wouldn't say my mood has changed. I'm generally a pretty upbeat person. My mom always used to say I was her sunshine child, which is sweet, but she also used to say that about my brother, so I don't know how special it really is. He actually just got a new dog, by the way. A golden retriever puppy. They named him Buster. He is so cute, but oh my gosh, the chewing! He chewed right through my brother's favorite pair of leather loafers. The ones he bought in Italy when he went for his honeymoon. They went to Rome and Florence, and he said the pasta was just incredible. I've always wanted to go to Italy, especially since my husband's family is from there. We were supposed to go for our tenth anniversary, but then our roof started leaking and we had to spend all our savings on getting it fixed. The contractor we hired was such a nightmare, too. He kept showing up late and leaving his tools all over the lawn. I nearly tripped over a hammer when I was taking the trash out one morning. It was so dangerous! But... wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Mood? Yeah, no, my mood is fine. Just normal, I guess.
Do you find it hard to focus on tasks or pay attention to what's going on around you?

Um, focus? Yeah, I definitely have a hard time with that. Like at the office, if I'm trying to type up an email or something, literally anything can throw me off. If a phone rings, or if people are talking nearby, or even if I just have a random thought about something I need to do at home, my brain just completely abandons what I was working on. It's so annoying. Speaking of things at home, I keep meaning to clean out the gutters before it snows. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he fell off his ladder last year trying to do his gutters. Broke his collarbone! He was in this huge sling for weeks. His wife had to drive him everywhere, and she is a terrible driver. I rode with her once to a bake sale, and she completely blew through a stop sign. Didn't even slow down. I was clutching the door handle the whole time. We were bringing these lemon bars I made—they're my grandmother's recipe, actually. You have to use real lemon juice, none of that bottled stuff, or they taste artificial. I always buy the big bag of lemons from Costco. Do you shop at Costco? They have those massive muffins, but honestly, they're more like cake. I try not to buy them because I'll eat the whole pack in three days. But... wait, what was the question? Focus? Yeah, I just get pulled away from my work really easily.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or pain lately?

Headaches? Um, no, not really. I mean, my body feels fine. I don't really get headaches, thank goodness. My sister gets migraines, though, and they sound awful. She has to go lie down in a dark room with a cold washcloth over her eyes for hours. Sometimes she even throws up from the pain. It started when she was pregnant with her second kid, my nephew Leo. He's the one who plays soccer now. He just made the travel team, which is a huge commitment. My sister spends every weekend driving him to tournaments all over the state. They were just in Ohio last weekend, and she said the hotel they stayed at didn't even have a working ice machine. Can you imagine? You pay all that money for a room and you can't even get ice for your water bottle. I always travel with my own insulated cup anyway, the kind that keeps ice frozen for like two days. I bought it on Amazon after seeing a video about it online. The girl in the video dropped it out of her car window and it didn't even dent! I haven't dropped mine yet, but it's good to know it's durable. I got it in this really pretty teal color. But, um... wait, what did you ask me? Pain? Oh, right. No, no headaches or anything like that. I feel perfectly fine physically.
Have you had trouble remembering how to do things you've done many times before, like a hobby or a routine task?

Remembering how to do things? Um, no, I don't think I have trouble with that. Like, I know *how* to do my job and my hobbies and stuff. I love to crochet, actually. I've been crocheting since my grandma taught me when I was ten. I'm making a baby blanket right now for my coworker, Sarah. She's due in November. It's her first, a little boy, and they're doing a whole woodland creature theme for the nursery. Fox wallpaper, little plush bears, it's adorable. I found this really soft yarn at the craft store that's supposed to be hypoallergenic, which is good because you never know with babies. My cousin's baby broke out in hives from a laundry detergent once. They had to switch to that special unscented kind, the one in the white bottle? It's so expensive, though. Everything is so expensive right now. I went to the grocery store yesterday just for milk and eggs and somehow spent forty dollars. And they didn't even have the brand of coffee creamer I like. I usually get the hazelnut one, but they only had French vanilla, which just tastes like melted marshmallows to me. I ended up getting it anyway because I can't drink black coffee. It's too bitter. My husband drinks it black, though. I don't know how he does it. But, um... wait, what were we talking about? Hobbies? Oh, right, forgetting how to do things. No, I remember how to do things just fine. I just forget where I put my crochet hook half the time!
Do you find that your mind jumps from one topic to another when you're talking or thinking?

Jumping from one topic to another? Hmm. No, I don't really think I do that. I feel like my conversations flow pretty normally. Like, I talk a lot with the vendors at work—I'm a secretary, so I handle all the incoming calls and stuff. The guy who delivers our office supplies, Dave, he's always telling me about his dog. It's a golden retriever mix named Buster. Buster just had to have surgery because he ate a whole pair of socks. Can you believe that? A whole pair! The vet bills were astronomical. Vets are so expensive nowadays. I took my cat, Mittens, in for just a regular checkup and it was over a hundred dollars. And she didn't even need shots! She was so mad at me for putting her in the carrier, she hid under the couch for two days straight. We had to lure her out with tuna. Not the cheap kind either, she only likes the solid white albacore. My husband says we spoil her, but she's just a picky eater. He's picky too, honestly. He refuses to eat any vegetable that's green, except for peas. But only if they're mixed into mashed potatoes. It's like feeding a toddler sometimes. Anyway, wait... what were we just talking about? Jumping topics? Oh, right. No, I don't think my mind really does that. I usually just stick to whatever I'm talking about.
Do you ever feel mentally foggy or like you're in a daze?

Mentally foggy? Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't feel like I'm in a daze or anything. I feel pretty clear-headed most of the time. Actually, speaking of being in a daze, you know what really makes me feel weird? That allergy medicine, the one in the little pink pills. I took that once when the pollen was really bad last spring. The oak trees in our neighborhood were just coating everything in this thick yellow dust. You couldn't even see the windshield of my car. I had to run it through the car wash twice in one week. The car wash on Main Street is usually pretty good, but they raised their prices again. It used to be eight dollars for the basic wash, and now it's twelve. Twelve dollars just for soap and water! And the vacuums there hardly ever work right. The suction is always terrible. My husband tried to vacuum out his truck there last month after a camping trip, and it wouldn't even pick up the pine needles. They went up to the mountains, near that big lake, I can't remember the name of it. He caught a couple of trout, but he said the mosquitoes were absolutely vicious. He forgot the bug spray, of course. I always pack it when we go together, but he packed his own bag this time. He bought this new fancy cooler for the trip, one of those ones that's supposed to be bear-proof. Like we have bears around here anyway! But he insisted he needed it. Wait, what did you ask me? Being in a daze? Oh, right. No, I don't get foggy or anything like that. I feel totally fine in that department.
Do you ever find yourself struggling to find the right words when you're trying to explain something?

Struggling to find the right words? Um, no, not really. I'm usually pretty quick with coming up with what I need to say. I mean, I talk all day at work, explaining things to callers and the new hires. Like, just yesterday I had to explain our new phone system to the temp. We got these new digital phones, and they are way too complicated. There are like fifty buttons on the console. I don't know why we couldn't just keep the old ones. The old ones were perfectly fine. But our office manager, Linda, she went to this tech seminar in Chicago and came back obsessed with "modernizing" the front desk. 

Chicago is supposed to be beautiful, though. I've never been, but my sister went there for her anniversary last year. They went to that big bean statue and took pictures. She said the pizza there is incredible, like super thick crust. I love thick crust pizza. The place down the street from our house makes a really good deep dish, but they always skimp on the pepperoni. If I'm paying twenty-two dollars for a pizza, I want it covered in pepperoni, you know? My husband says I complain too much about it, but it's the principle of the thing. We usually order from them on Friday nights when we're too tired to cook. By Friday, I just don't want to look at a stove. 

Anyway... wait, what were we talking about? Finding words? Oh, right. No, I don't really struggle with that. I always know what I want to say.
Do you ever find yourself having trouble remembering specific words or names when you're in the middle of a conversation?

Trouble remembering words or names? Hmm. No, I don't think so. I'm usually pretty good with names. I have to be, right? Answering the phones all day, you get to know everybody. Like Mr. Henderson, he calls every Tuesday at 10 AM sharp for my boss. He's this older gentleman, very polite, always asks how my day is going. He has this really deep, booming voice, almost like a radio announcer. It reminds me of my grandfather. My grandfather used to listen to those old radio shows, the mysteries and stuff, on AM radio. He had this huge antique radio in his living room, a big wooden cabinet thing. It was gorgeous. My aunt has it now, she took it after he passed away. She's always collecting antiques. Her house is just packed with old furniture and knick-knacks. Honestly, it feels a little cluttered to me, but she loves it. She goes to estate sales every weekend looking for bargains. She found this beautiful vintage tea set last month, floral pattern, perfectly intact. I'm not really a tea person, though. I need my coffee in the morning, or I'm completely useless. Just one cup, but it has to be strong. French roast, usually. 

Wait, what was the question? Forgetting names? Oh, yeah, no. I don't really have a problem with that. I remember names and words just fine.
Do you often feel unusually tired or lacking in energy?

Unusually tired? Um, no, I wouldn't say that. I usually have plenty of energy. I mean, I stay pretty busy at the front desk, so I don't really have time to be tired! We did just get a new coffee machine in the breakroom, though, which helps. One of those fancy pod ones. Management made this big deal about it being a reward for hitting our quarterly goals, but then they only buy the cheapest, most bitter coffee pods for it. My coworker, Brenda, she actually started bringing in her own herbal tea bags because she refuses to drink it. 

Brenda is so funny about her tea. She has this special ceramic mug with a little lid to keep it warm. She knocked it over on her keyboard last month, though, and it was a whole disaster. IT had to come up and replace the whole setup. The IT guy, Kevin, he was so annoyed. He's always complaining about how far he has to walk from his office in the basement. The basement down there is so creepy, honestly. It always smells like old cardboard and floor wax. I had to go down there once to find some archived files from a few years ago, and the fluorescent lights kept flickering. It felt exactly like the start of a horror movie. I told my boss I am never going down there by myself again, he can send the temp next time. 

Wait, sorry, what were we just talking about? Being tired? Oh! Right. No, I don't feel lacking in energy or anything. I feel pretty normal.
Do you find yourself having trouble recalling specific words when you're speaking, even if you know what you want to say?

Trouble recalling specific words? Didn't you just ask me that? Or was it about names? I feel like we just went over this. No, I don't really have that problem. I always know what I'm trying to say. My husband, though, he does that all the time. He'll be in the middle of a sentence and just stop, snapping his fingers trying to remember a word. It drives me crazy. Like last night, we were watching this documentary about deep sea diving, and he was trying to think of the word for submarine, but he kept calling it a "water boat." A water boat! I couldn't stop laughing. 

That documentary was fascinating, though. They went all the way down to the Mariana Trench. Did you know there are fish down there that glow in the dark? It's bioluminescence or something. It looks so alien. I can't imagine being in a tiny little sub that deep underwater. The pressure would be terrifying. I get claustrophobic just being in the elevator at work if there are more than five people in it. Our building is so old, the elevator creaks and groans every time it stops at a floor. It got stuck between the second and third floor for twenty minutes last month, and Linda—the office manager—she was in there. She was practically having a panic attack by the time maintenance got the doors open. 

Anyway... yeah. No trouble with words here. I think my memory for that kind of stuff is perfectly fine.
Do you often pause or struggle to find the right words when speaking to someone?

Wait, are you asking me about words again? I swear you just asked me that like two minutes ago. Are you testing me or something? Because my memory is totally fine! But you know who does repeat themselves constantly? My boss, Mr. Davis. He will come out of his office and ask me if I ordered the printer toner, and then twenty minutes later, he's back at my desk asking the exact same thing. It’s like, yes, Mr. Davis, I ordered the toner. We go through so much of it, too, because he insists on printing out every single email. Who prints emails anymore? It's such a waste of paper. 

I try to tell him we need to go paperless, it's better for the environment. I actually just started really getting into recycling at home. I got those separate bins for plastics and cardboard and everything. The recycling truck comes on Thursdays, but they come so early, like 6 AM, and the truck is so incredibly loud it wakes up my neighbor's dog. That dog barks at absolutely everything. It’s a little terrier mix, super cute, but man, it has a set of lungs on it. It barked at the mailman for ten straight minutes yesterday. I felt so bad for the guy, he was just trying to drop off a package on the porch and this little dog is just going ballistic through the screen door. 

Wait, what were we... oh, right. Pausing when I speak. No, I really don't do that. Like I said, I don't have any trouble finding words. I talk just fine, I promise!
Do you ever find yourself unable to recall a specific word you know, even if you can describe what it means?

Are we seriously doing this again? I feel like I'm in the Twilight Zone or something! You've literally asked me about finding words like three times now. I don't mean to be rude, but are you reading off a script or something? Because my answer hasn't changed. No, I don't forget words. 

My sister, though, she does that thing where she describes the word instead of just saying it. Like, she'll say "the thing you use to cut the grass" instead of lawnmower. She's always been a little spacey, though. She used to forget her lunchbox on the bus at least once a week when we were kids. My mom got so mad she started making her buy lunch at the cafeteria, which was awful because our school cafeteria served these weird, square pizzas that tasted like cardboard. I actually saw square pizza at the grocery store the other day and it gave me a total flashback. I was in the frozen aisle looking for those little mini quiches—the spinach and feta ones, they're so good for a quick breakfast. But they were completely sold out. 

The grocery store has been a mess lately anyway, they're remodeling the whole produce section. It's so dusty in there, I sneezed like five times just trying to pick out some apples. I usually get Honeycrisp, but they only had Granny Smith, which are way too tart for me. I guess they're good for baking, but who has time to bake a pie? 

Anyway, sorry, I know you're just doing your job. But no, to answer your question for the fourth time, I don't have any trouble remembering words.
Do you ever feel like you're not thinking as clearly as you usually do?

Not thinking clearly? Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, my brain feels like it's working the way it always does. I'm always pretty sharp, especially at work. You have to be when you're managing the front desk and juggling four different phone lines. Though, honestly, the phones have been a little quieter this week because half the office is out with that stomach bug that's been going around. 

It's awful, Linda caught it first and she was out for three days. She came back looking so pale. I've been wiping down my desk with those Clorox wipes like a madwoman because I cannot afford to get sick right now. My husband and I are supposed to go to his parents' house for their anniversary this weekend, and his mother is already so particular about everything. If we don't show up, she'll hold it against us until Christmas. Last year we were late for Thanksgiving dinner because of traffic on the interstate—there was this huge accident with a semi-truck carrying, like, a million cabbages or something, they were all over the road—and she made little passive-aggressive comments about it all through dessert. 

So yeah, I'm taking vitamin C and drinking tons of water. You really have to stay hydrated. But anyway, what were you asking? Oh, thinking clearly. Yeah, no, I feel fine. My head is clear. No problems there.
Do you ever find yourself knowing what you want to say, but unable to think of the exact word to use?

Okay, is this a prank? Are there hidden cameras in here? Because I feel like I'm losing my mind—you literally just asked me this! Knowing what I want to say but not finding the exact word... no! Like I just said, I don't have that problem. I always know the exact word. 

I'm actually the one who proofreads everything at the office before it goes out, so I'm pretty good with words. You wouldn't believe the typos people make. Just yesterday, one of the sales guys, Greg, sent out a mass email and he spelled 'definitely' with an 'a'. Defiantly! It completely changes the whole meaning of the sentence! I had to run over to his cubicle and tell him to recall the email. Greg is nice, but he's always rushing through everything. He drinks like four energy drinks a day, those giant cans with the neon logos on them. I don't know how his heart doesn't just explode. 

I tried one of those once when I was studying for my finals in high school, and my hands were shaking so bad I couldn't even hold my pencil. I strictly stick to coffee now. Just one cup in the morning with a little almond milk. The vanilla kind, not the unsweetened one. The unsweetened one tastes like actual chalk. I bought it by accident last week because the labels look exactly the same, and I had to pour my whole mug down the sink. 

But anyway... yeah. No. I don't get stuck on words. I promise you, my vocabulary is completely fine and we can move on to a different topic!
Can you tell me the name of the object you use to write with?

A pen? Or a pencil, I guess. I usually use a pen, though. Blue ink, specifically. I can't stand black ink, it just looks so harsh on the paper, you know? We have these really nice gel pens at the front desk, the kind that glide so smoothly when you write. I had to special order them because the standard office supply catalog only had those cheap ballpoint ones that always dry up after two days. 

It took me like three weeks of nagging the office manager to approve the order. She's so stingy with the budget. She wouldn't even approve getting a new microwave for the breakroom after the old one started making this horrible buzzing noise. It sounds like a giant hornet is trapped inside it. I won't even heat up my lunch in there anymore, I've just been bringing salads. Which is fine, I guess, I'm trying to eat healthier anyway. But sometimes you just really want a warm bowl of soup, especially since they keep the AC blasting in the lobby. I have to wear a cardigan even in July. 

But yeah, a pen. That's what I use.
Can you think of a time when you knew what you wanted to say but couldn't think of the right word to use?

Wait, are you... are you reading from a broken script or something? I literally just answered this like two minutes ago! No! I cannot think of a time, because it doesn't happen to me. 

I swear, it's like talking to my husband. I'll tell him something, clear as day, and five minutes later he'll ask me the exact same question. Just last night, I told him we needed to leave by 6:00 for his parents' anniversary thing this weekend, and he just nods, right? Completely zoned out, staring at the TV. He was watching this documentary about deep-sea fish. Those anglerfish with the little glowing lights on their heads? They are so creepy looking, honestly, they look like actual aliens. I don't know how anyone can watch that right before bed. It would give me nightmares. I had a nightmare once that I was trapped in a submarine, which is weird because I'm not even claustrophobic, but it was so dark and the water pressure was making this creaking sound... 

But anyway, what I'm saying is, no. I don't forget words. I just told you that. Are you actually writing down my answers, or are we just going to keep going in circles?

We tried to get him to come ice skating with us, but he said his ankles were too weak. Weak ankles! Can you imagine? He's fourteen! Broke his collarbone! He was in this huge sling for weeks. His wife had to drive him everywhere, and she is a terrible driver. I rode with her once to a bake sale, and she completely blew through a stop sign. Didn't even slow down. I was clutching the door handle the whole time. We were bringing these lemon bars I made—they're my grandmother's recipe, actually. You have to use real lemon juice, none of that bottled stuff, or they taste artificial. I always buy the big bag of lemons from Costco. Do you shop at Costco? They have those massive muffins, but honestly, they're more like cake. I try not to buy them because I'll eat the whole pack in three days. But... wait, what was the question? Focus? Yeah, I just get pulled away from my work really easily.

You pay all that money for a room and you can't even get ice for your water bottle. I always travel with my own insulated cup anyway, the kind that keeps ice frozen for like two days. I bought it on Amazon after seeing a video about it online. The girl in the video dropped it out of her car window and it didn't even dent! I haven't dropped mine yet, but it's good to know it's durable. I got it in this really pretty teal color. But, um... wait, what did you ask me? Pain? Oh, right. No, no headaches or anything like that. I feel perfectly fine physically.

I found this really soft yarn at the craft store that's supposed to be hypoallergenic, which is good because you never know with babies. I usually get the hazelnut one, but they only had French vanilla, which just tastes like melted marshmallows to me. I ended up getting it anyway because I can't drink black coffee. It's too bitter. My husband drinks it black, though. I don't know how he does it. But, um... wait, what were we talking about? Hobbies? Oh, right, forgetting how to do things. She was so mad at me for putting her in the carrier, she hid under the couch for two days straight. We had to lure her out with tuna. Not the cheap kind either, she only likes the solid white albacore. My husband says we spoil her, but she's just a picky eater. He's picky too, honestly. He refuses to eat any vegetable that's green, except for peas. But only if they're mixed into mashed potatoes. It's like feeding a toddler sometimes. Anyway, wait... what were we just talking about? Jumping topics? Oh, right. No, I don't think my mind really does that. I usually just stick to whatever I'm talking about.

The oak trees in our neighborhood were just coating everything in this thick yellow dust. You couldn't even see the windshield of my car. I had to run it through the car wash twice in one week. The car wash on Main Street is usually pretty good, but they raised their prices again. It used to be eight dollars for the basic wash, and now it's twelve. Twelve dollars just for soap and water! And the vacuums there hardly ever work right. The suction is always terrible. My husband tried to vacuum out his truck there last month after a camping trip, and it wouldn't even pick up the pine needles. They went up to the mountains, near that big lake, I can't remember the name of it. He caught a couple of trout, but he said the mosquitoes were absolutely vicious. He forgot the bug spray, of course. I always pack it when we go together, but he packed his own bag this time. He bought this new fancy cooler for the trip, one of those ones that's supposed to be bear-proof. Like we have bears around here anyway! But he insisted he needed it. Wait, what did you ask me? Being in a daze? Oh, right. No, I don't get foggy or anything like that. I feel totally fine in that department.

But our office manager, Linda, she went to this tech seminar in Chicago and came back obsessed with "modernizing" the front desk. 

Chicago is supposed to be beautiful, though. I've never been, but my sister went there for her anniversary last year. They went to that big bean statue and took pictures. She said the pizza there is incredible, like super thick crust. I love thick crust pizza. The place down the street from our house makes a really good deep dish, but they always skimp on the pepperoni. If I'm paying twenty-two dollars for a pizza, I want it covered in pepperoni, you know? My husband says I complain too much about it, but it's the principle of the thing. We usually order from them on Friday nights when we're too tired to cook. By Friday, I just don't want to look at a stove. 

Anyway... wait, what were we talking about? Finding words? Oh, right. No, I don't really struggle with that. I always know what I want to say.

Her house is just packed with old furniture and knick-knacks. Honestly, it feels a little cluttered to me, but she loves it. She goes to estate sales every weekend looking for bargains. She found this beautiful vintage tea set last month, floral pattern, perfectly intact. I'm not really a tea person, though. I need my coffee in the morning, or I'm completely useless. Just one cup, but it has to be strong. French roast, usually. 

Wait, what was the question? Forgetting names? Oh, yeah, no. I don't really have a problem with that. I remember names and words just fine.

The basement down there is so creepy, honestly. It always smells like old cardboard and floor wax. I had to go down there once to find some archived files from a few years ago, and the fluorescent lights kept flickering. It felt exactly like the start of a horror movie. I told my boss I am never going down there by myself again, he can send the temp next time. 

Wait, sorry, what were we just talking about? Being tired? Oh! Right. No, I don't feel lacking in energy or anything. I feel pretty normal.

She was practically having a panic attack by the time maintenance got the doors open.

The recycling truck comes on Thursdays, but they come so early, like 6 AM, and the truck is so incredibly loud it wakes up my neighbor's dog. That dog barks at absolutely everything. I felt so bad for the guy, he was just trying to drop off a package on the porch and this little dog is just going ballistic through the screen door.

My husband and I are supposed to go to his parents' house for their anniversary this weekend, and his mother is already so particular about everything.
